references.summary:
I found 6 live references, all checked in a headless browser or by fetching their HTML on 27 Sep 2026. Frames are saved as WebP files of 7–97 KB under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-logink/a373dafe-cad0-44b3-be23-c6da0cb9f694/scratchpad/blueprint/references/<site>/best-*.webp. The six:
(a) Terminal Industries: a canvas sequence of WebP frames. It shows the mechanism to copy and a budget to avoid: 400 frames, about 22 MB on desktop.
(b) AirOps: a sticky visual stage beside a readable list whose active item changes as you scroll.
(c) iPullRank: condensed-caps headlines plus a monospace font, on a site selling AI-search services.
(d) Linear: its product screens are real HTML, labelled like figures in a technical document.
(e) Rivian: a film hero that loads its still first. The still is frame 0 of the same clip, with a separate portrait crop for phones. Apple's AirPods Pro 3 page is added as a supplement for its preload settings, its load timeout and its visible pause button.
(f) Profound: an AI answer that streams in word by word, plus a map of the sources AI engines cite. It also shows what not to do: an H1 stuffed with engine names, and text hidden until you scroll.
I found one real defect in the chosen direction. It never gives the looping 8 s hero film a visible pause control, and the crawler-log ticker only pauses on hover. WCAG 2.2.2 (level A) requires a way to pause both. The fix is in the sections below. The rest of the direction's rules hold up against these references.

references.ingredients: (a) Apple-style scroll-scrubbed canvas image sequence; also Lenis smooth scroll and a pinned hero
references.what_to_learn: Checked live 27 Sep 2026. The hero is a 2D <canvas>. It draws WebP frames loaded as blob URLs, driven by GSAP ScrollTrigger and Lenis (the html element carries class 'lenis'). Desktop and phone get separate frame sets, named /static/frames/home/{desktop|mobile}/webp/hero_anim_{desktop|mobile}_60_{0..399}.webp. Desktop is 400 frames, about 22 MB at 57 KB each on average. Mobile is 400 frames, about 12 MB at 31 KB each. Frames are fetched out of order: the first ones, then ones near the end, then the middle, so the whole range appears early and fills in (coarse-to-fine). The subject is one locked-off vehicle moving through dusk light, the same device as a day passing over one rooftop. The three captions are real server-rendered text (<h2 class='title title-sequence'>), which is good. The costs are high, though: the captions sit on top of the frames, Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) is that H2 at 5.4–6.9 s, and headless probes measured cumulative layout shift (CLS) of about 1.0. Copy the pipeline and the drama; avoid the ~10× budget, frames on phones, text over frames and the CLS.
references.how_logink_adapts:
The Overture 'Satu atap, satu hari' keeps the mechanism and drops the excess. It uses 120 frames at 1280×720 WebP q62–68, capped at 2.5 MB in total, with the pre-committed fallbacks: 96 frames, then q60, then 1120w. Name the frames rooftop-000.webp to rooftop-119.webp. Load them only after window load and only within one viewport, in coarse-to-fine order (0, 119, 60, 30, 90 …). Decode with createImageBitmap inside a byte-budgeted window and release frames offscreen. The canvas tier needs a fine pointer and a width of at least 1024px. Phones get 4 keyframes at 600×800 (about 35 KB each), crossfaded by CSS view-timelines, with no canvas JS at all. Captions never go over frames: the
    of four

  1. sits in a flat Kertas column, and the canvas is aria-hidden over the server-rendered poster . The runway is calc(4 × min(100svh, 900px)). Add one CI assertion Terminal shows is needed: CLS ≤0.05 at 1440 with the canvas tier active, not only on the static path.

references.site: AirOps ('Research that shapes how the category thinks' section)
references.ingredients: (b) pinned storytelling: a sticky stage whose visual swaps as scroll steps advance; AI-citation research used as proof
references.what_to_learn: On the left, a sticky stage shows research pages and a heatmap of citation share. It swaps as the list on the right advances. The active item expands, marked by a green bar about 4px wide, with a one-line finding that carries a number ('53% of fintech ChatGPT answers now carry an ad, up from near zero in April') and a link. Inactive items collapse to grey titles. ScrollTrigger drives three segments of about 675px each with no JS pin: the stickiness comes from a CSS sticky wrapper. All three item titles are in the server HTML. The ground is flat paper and no text sits on the visual. The lesson: the list is the readable, crawlable spine and the stage is secondary. Each step is a sentence with a number.
references.how_logink_adapts:
This maps one-to-one onto the Overture and onto the service-page section 'Apa yang kami kerjakan'. The stage is min(100svh, 900px) tall in columns 8–12 and holds the rooftop canvas and the live-HTML phone. A flat Kertas
    sits in columns 1–7. The IntersectionObserver sets data-step, and the active
  1. gets a 3px rule in its stage key light (magenta, crimson, coral, Jingga). This is AirOps' green bar recoloured by the ribbon. Two differences from AirOps: inactive steps stay fully legible in Aspal 70 (8.25:1 on Kertas), and every 40–60-word

    stays open and visible, never collapsed. The phone screen crossfades in 240ms. Use descriptive anchors in place of AirOps' 'Learn more', per the SEO rules.

references.ingredients: (c) editorial condensed-caps typography on the web; monospace technical labels; category peer (AI-search agency)
references.what_to_learn: The server-rendered H1 is 'BE RECOMMENDED BY AI AND REMEMBERED BY PEOPLE': one H1 set as two lines of the same condensed face, a light line over a heavy line, so the emphasis comes from weight rather than colour. The face is Oswald from Google Fonts, with only weights 300 and 400 requested; check whether the heavy line is being faux-bolded. Service cards use condensed-caps names ('AI SEARCH', 'TECHNICAL SEO') over JetBrains Mono copy, with '//.services_001' code-style labels. The takeaway is that condensed caps plus mono reads as 'technical editorial' for an SEO/AI agency, at 4–6 words per line. Weak points: a centred H1, third-party render-blocking Google Fonts CSS, mono used for body text, and an orange/yellow button palette.
references.how_logink_adapts: Logink makes the same move with one self-hosted Archivo variable file (90,096 B, next/font, preloaded), where the width axis does the work. Title lines are wdth 62, wght 850, caps. The single 'Kata Lebar' line ('DIKUTIP AI.') is wdth 125, wght 300; it plays the role of iPullRank's light line. Lines are left-set, one nowrap span each, with a size-adjusted Roboto Condensed / Arial Narrow fallback. Caps appear only on the home H1 and the four chapter titles; service H1s are sentence case at wdth 74. Martian Mono stays inside the instruments (crawler log, JSON-LD, prompt table) and never carries body copy. One differentiation warning: globally, 'condensed caps + mono + orange CTA' already belongs to iPullRank. Logink's distinction has to come from the datelines, the clock numerals in ribbon key lights, the paper/plum/indigo grounds and WhatsApp green. So keep Jingga off button fills on paper (already banned), and add no '//code' labels, keeping the cap of three motifs.

references.ingredients: (d) live-HTML technical interface details and product-UI motion
references.what_to_learn: The hero product UI is live DOM: the server HTML contains 'Faster app launch', 'vehicle_state' and 'Triage Intelligence'. It stays crisp at any DPR, and an assistant panel types its message in client-side. Further down, tiny mono captions ('FIG 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3') label hairline isometric line drawings over column rules, and a two-tone paragraph sets a white lead sentence against a grey continuation. The register is a technical document. The motion is small: typed text and state changes, never a video of the UI. One caveat: a headless probe on 26 Sep recorded Linear's desktop LCP as a 2560w image, so not every visual there is DOM.
references.how_logink_adapts: Author every instrument once as live HTML/CSS, with no WebM twins (owner decision 10). That covers SERP → Maps pack, the Instagram grid and review card, the website frame, ad → WhatsApp, and the Bab III 'Di balik layar' set: AI answer card with numbered citations, prompt table, share-of-voice bars, crawler log, JSON-LD and query fan-out. Build them on Senja Dalam or Kertas with 0-radius panels and rgba hairlines. Server-render the text and animate it once on data-in: words at 45ms each capped at 600ms, bars by scaleX, transform only. Linear's mocks show its own real product; Logink's are illustrations. So in place of FIG labels, the one label is 'ILUSTRASI · DATA CONTOH' in Archivo expanded caps, the mock is wrapped in data-nosnippet, and it carries no third-party chrome and no '2min ago'-style stamps (the narrative-clock rule). Keep the H1 as LCP, with instruments below the fold.

references.site: Rivian (homepage film hero), with Apple AirPods Pro 3 as a supplement
references.what_to_learn: Rivian's markup is a good poster-first pattern. A <picture> holds art-directed stills per breakpoint: a portrait crop up to 744px and landscape above. Both are cut from the same Cloudinary video asset at so_0 (start offset 0), so the still is exactly frame 0 and the swap to video is invisible. After it comes <video playsinline muted loop autoplay preload='none'> with media-queried <source>s from 720w up to 4200w, delivered as f_auto:video. The phone screenshot confirms the portrait crop. Its weaknesses against Logink's rules: the headline and CTAs sit on the moving film, and phones download video. Apple's AirPods Pro 3 page (apple.com/airpods-pro, checked the same day) supplies the missing controls. It uses <video preload='none' role='img' aria-label>, server-rendered startframe/endframe images, and the plugins ViewportSourceOnce, LoadTimeout (3000 ms, after which it stays on the still) and PlayPauseButton, which shows as a visible pause button on the hero. Frame: apple-airpods-pro/best-poster-pause-control.webp.
references.how_logink_adapts: In 'Buka', the headline sits on flat Putih above and the 21:9 film runs full-bleed below. The poster is a 1280w WebP of 80 KB or less, set to fetchpriority high. Make it frame 0 of the final VP9 encode rather than the Nano Banana still, so the grade matches exactly. Phones get a separate 4:3 crop of 60 KB or less through <picture media> and no <video> source at all. The video element is <video muted playsinline loop preload='none' aria-hidden>, and its src is attached only after window load, only in view, and never under Save-Data, reduced motion or Mode teks. Add Apple's 3 s load timeout, after which the poster stays, and fade the film in on 'playing'. Also add Apple's visible pause button: see the defect section.

references.ingredients: (f) AI-search marketing presenting AI answers and citations
references.what_to_learn:
Profound presents AI search as working product. The hero is an 'AI Marketer' conversation UI in live DOM (the server HTML contains 'Wrenfield' and 'battery life and health'). Its answer streams in word by word behind a blur front, under a 'Working 6s' status. A later section draws a 'constellation' of cited source domains joined by hairlines. Section heads name the deliverables: 'Know what people are asking AI', 'Understand what AI says back', 'Verify the accuracy of AI claims'. Anti-patterns to avoid:
- The H1 rotator puts every engine name into the H1 text ('…win in ChatGPT Perplexity Claude Gemini Microsoft Copilot DeepSeek Google AI Overviews AI search platforms') through invisible opacity-0 blur spans.
- Section heads reveal with a scroll-scrubbed blur, so the text is invisible at rest (frame profound/best-blur-reveal-hidden-text.webp).
- Third-party logos appear inside the art.
- The black-on-black look is generic SaaS.
references.how_logink_adapts:
Bab III 'Di balik layar' takes the streaming answer and the cited sources, localises them and labels them honestly:
- The question is 'Kopi susu enak di Tebet yang buka sampai malam?'.
- The answer is server-rendered word spans, revealed transform-only (no blur filter) at 45ms per word, capped at 600ms.
- Numbered chips (1)(2)(3) follow, with (2) contohkedai.id ringed in Jingga.
- Engines appear as plain Martian Mono text chips (ChatGPT · Gemini · AI Mode · Perplexity), never as logos.
- The Proof Loupe reveals how each deliverable is measured.
The constellation becomes the query fan-out instrument, built in live HTML rather than WebGL. The H1 stays the exact approved string, enforced by the CI textContent test. The proof is Logink's own honest baseline, 'logink.co: 1 kutipan AI (Ahrefs, Sep 2026)', never a vendor's statistics.

sections.title: Defect found in the chosen direction: no pause control on looping motion (WCAG 2.2.2, level A)
sections.body_markdown:
final.md covers the hero film loop and the crawler-log ticker only in these places:
- lines 173 and 631: the 8 s film `loop` 'pauses offscreen and on visibilitychange'
- line 284: the crawler-log ticker 'pauses on hover and under reduced motion'

Neither gives users a visible way to pause. Both start on their own, run for more than 5 s and play alongside other content, so WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide) requires a pause mechanism. Hover does not count, because keyboard and touch users cannot hover. Apple's AirPods Pro 3 hero shows the standard fix: a visible PlayPauseButton.

**Fix (binding amendment):**
- **Film:** put a `<button type="button" aria-pressed>` labelled 'Jeda film' / 'Lanjutkan film' (EN 'Pause film' / 'Play film') at the right end of the film's caption line. The caption sits on flat Putih, so the button is not on the film and the no-text-on-imagery rule holds. Make it a 44px target with a 2px Aspal focus ring. It lives inside the desktop-only FilmLoop island, so phones, which get no video, ship 0 KB for it. Store the choice in sessionStorage, with try/catch around every read and write.
  - Do not use the label 'Putar film'. The phase-2 cursor label 'Putar film (0:45)' already uses it.
- **Crawler ticker:** add the same toggle, or pause it on `:focus-within` plus a 'Jeda' button. The Mode teks checkbox beside it counts as a 'hide' mechanism, so a small ticker toggle closes the gap.
- **Phone poster push-in (12 s):** run it once and stop, never loop it.

**Two small tightenings (not defects):**
1. Rivian cuts its poster from the same asset at `so_0`. Do the same: extract Logink's poster from the final encode, not the source still. Command: `ffmpeg -i hero.webm -frames:v 1 -vf scale=1280:-2 poster.png && /usr/local/bin/cwebp -q 72 poster.png -o hero-poster-1280.webp`. ffmpeg still has to be installed (Phase 0). This guarantees the 'swap is invisible' requirement.
2. Terminal Industries measured CLS of about 1.0 with its sequence. Add a CI run that measures CLS with the canvas tier active at 1440 (≤0.05), not only on the static and phone paths.

sections.title: What the references confirm (no change to the direction)
sections.body_markdown:
- **Canvas budget:** Terminal ships 400 desktop frames (about 22 MB) and 400 phone frames (about 12 MB). Final.md's 120 frames at ≤2.5 MB, desktop only, is about 9× lighter, and the fallback ladder (96 frames, then q60, then 1120w) is sound.
- **Nothing on frames or film:** Terminal, Rivian and Profound all put text on moving imagery or hide text until scroll. Final.md's flat-surface rule is the better choice for readability, crawlers and CLS.
- **Steps stay in the DOM:** AirOps proves the sticky-stage-plus-list pattern reads well. Final.md goes further, keeping every step's paragraph open and visible.
- **H1 text check:** Profound's rotator stuffs 8 engine names into its H1. The CI test `h1.textContent === approved string` is justified.
- **UI as live HTML:** Linear and Profound both ship their product UI as server-rendered DOM rather than video. That confirms owner decision 10.
- **Condensed caps in the category:** iPullRank shows condensed caps plus mono already reads as 'AI search agency'. Logink should rely on its datelines, ribbon key lights and paper to stay distinct, and must not add a fourth motif.
